correctness.rationale: The backward equations for h_(1,+), h_(1,−), h_(2,+), h_(2,−) use the stated four total count rates c,d, switching κ and absorbing counts 0 and 3. Their rational elimination gives Φ=a/A+(a−1)^2 G κ[cA+2(a²+1)κ]/(2AD), D>0. Direct rational 4×4 solves independently matched that formula in five strategically chosen parameter cases including a=1, κ=κ0, and c on both sides of 2d. Subtraction of 1/3 has the sign of (c−2d)Gκ−2aAcd, and the derivative quadratic has exactly one positive root when c>2d and none when c≤2d. For one transient count, the first absorption event takes place in some environment, so fixation is a convex mixture of frozen conditional probabilities. This is an algebraic all-parameter proof, not proof by finite grid.

The boundaries distinguish monotone neutral approach from genuine overshoot and unique optimum; the claim disclaims biological universality.

final_claim: In the specified reciprocal two-environment continuous-time birth–death model with three individuals, the two frozen fixation probabilities coincide at a/(a^2+a+1), every positive switching rate strictly improves fixation when a≠1, the response is monotone exactly when c≤2d, and for c>2d crosses neutral 1/3 once and has one finite optimum; size two cannot outperform the best frozen environment.
limitations: Applies only to the specified reciprocal count-dependent rates, independent symmetric switching and uniform initial environment; not general Moran fitness or arbitrary population sizes.
The five independent exact-rational samples corroborate but do not establish parameter-uniform identities; analytic backward elimination and signs supply the infinite family proof.
